rationales: findall does not overlap: the search resumes after the end of the match '123'.
'45' has only two digits and cannot match \d{3}.

items.q: Which texts does the pattern r'42?!' match?
rationales: That describes 42!?, where the exclamation mark is optional. In 42?! the question mark makes the 2 optional.
The 2 is optional, so '4!' matches as well.

options: A list of two tuples of three strings each
A list of two strings, the whole matches
A list of two Match objects
rationales: With groups in the pattern findall returns the group texts, not the whole matches.
findall returns strings or tuples of strings; finditer returns Match objects.
With exactly one group findall returns that group's text, not the whole match.
Tuples are returned only when the pattern has two or more groups.
That is the greedy <.*>; the question mark after the star makes it lazy.
A match must end with the closing angle bracket, so it cannot end after b.

items.q: What does re.sub(r'(\w)\w*', r'\1', 'spam eggs') return?
rationales: Every word is a match and is replaced by the text of group 1, its first letter.
Group 1 holds one character, (\w), so only one letter is kept.

items.q: What does re.search(r'^\d+$', '123\n') return in Python 3.14?
options: A match, because $ also fits just before a final newline
None, because $ requires the very end of the text
rationales: $ matches at the end or just before a newline that ends the text; \Z or fullmatch would require the very end.
A trailing newline is ordinary text; no error is raised.

options: None, because match looks only at the start of the text
A match with the empty string
rationales: That is what re.search finds; match does not scan forward.
The pattern is c, not an empty pattern, and it does not fit at position 0.

items.q: The chapter prints a match for re.compile('Eggs(and spam)+').search('Eggs and spam'). What do you get when you run that code?
options: None, because the pattern has no space before and
A match with span (0, 13), as the chapter prints
rationales: That is the result of 'Eggs( and spam)+'; the printed pattern lacks the space.
The plus requires at least one repetition, so 'Eggs' alone cannot match.

items.q: In the phone pattern of Project 3, findall returns tuples of nine strings. What is groups[6] for the text '415.555.9950 ext. 123'?
rationales: The digits are at index 8; index 6 is the outer extension group with its spaces and keyword.
The separators are at indexes 2 and 4.

items.q: How many matches does re.findall(r'\d', s) find when s is '1' followed by the Arabic-Indic digit three?
rationales: That is the count with re.ASCII or with [0-9]; \d alone accepts every Unicode decimal digit.
The ASCII digit 1 is matched in any case.
